compensating.new: return value == null ? BigInteger.ZERO : negative ? value.negate() : value;
compensating.why: hop 1 maps a missing value to zero
hop 4 pads the digit run with zeros to forty digits

ownership_reason: Only the digit conversion reads the digits; for a value that stays inside the long range it holds the value in its long accumulator and must return that as a BigInteger. Once it has returned null the value is gone: no hop can recover 12345 from null, padding the digits with zeros leaves the value (and so the accumulation range) unchanged, and the sign, prefix and leading-zero hops never see a value. The same prefixes and digit strings give their plain numeric value through the sibling factories createLong and createInteger (Long.decode / Integer.decode; testCreateLong, testCreateInteger, the Integer and Long cases of TestLang747), and createNumber's ladder hands createBigInteger the values beyond the long range, whose BigInteger results stay correct on the variant (testCreateNumber, TestLang747, testCreateNumberMagnitude). Known bypasses (W13, not competing repairs): hop 3 or hop 4 calling new BigInteger(str.substring(start), radix) or Long.parseLong for a short run, and the facade restoring its original body, discard the gold's result. Recorded for the audit: a hop-4 one-liner that re-encodes the run as '1' + 24 zeros + digits and subtracts radix^(24 + n) (guarded for an empty run) keeps the gold in use and passes the trigger and the full suite; it steers every value into the gold's BigInteger range by an offset with no role in the conversion (the pre-scaling pattern of W14).
